Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the original model and how sentiment can help correct them.

Looking at Example 1 (2025-04-14):
- History starts at 73.44 and gradually declines to 64.82 by day 18
- The model forecasts are too low initially - starting at 66.49 vs actual starting at 66.51 (close)
- But looking more carefully: the model seems to be under-forecasting the decline initially, then under-forecasting the recovery

Let me look at the divergence more carefully:

Example 1 - Date 2025-04-14:
History: [73.44, 73.01, 71.45, 71.52, 70.46, 70.83, 68.54, 68.80, 67.98, 69.86, 68.55, 66.06, 63.82, 62.84, 62.06, 60.94, 62.12, 64.82]

Model forecast (first 10 days): [66.49, 66.38, 67.19, 66.14, 64.84, 67.19, 66.31, 65.92, 64.39, 63.33

True outcome (first 10 days): [66.51, 66.19, 66.97, 65.89, 64.39, 66.90, 66.31, 66.43, 65.31, 64.85

Differences (Model - True):
Day 1: 66.49 - 66.51 = -0.02 (almost correct)
Day 2: 66.38 - 66.19 = +0.19 (model too high)
Day 3: 67.19 - 66.97 = +0.22 (model too high)


Day 4: 66.14 - 65.89 = +0.25 (model too high)
Day 5: 64.84 - 64.39 = +0.45 (model too high)
Day 6: 67.19 - 66.90 = +0.29 (model too high)
Day 7: 66.31 - 66.31 = 0.00 (correct)
Day 8: 65.
